text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between West Ham and Tottenham at London Stadium.

West Ham will be looking to bounce back from their disappointing 4-3 loss to Newcastle United in their previous Premier League outing, with the Hammers now winless in their last three top-flight outings.
David Moyes' men were in a strong position after goals from Michail Antonio, Mohammed Kudus, and Jarrod Bowen helped them come from behind to lead 3-1.
However, West Ham crumbled in the latter stages of the second half, with Newcastle scoring three times in 13 minutes to claim a precious victory.

The Irons will welcome a return to the London Stadium after collecting 24 points from their 15 matches at home and will attempt to turn their form around to ensure they qualify for European football next season.
West Ham are currently in seventh position, one point above Newcastle in eighth place and four behind Manchester United in sixth, with both teams having a game in hand.
Tottenham are pushing for a place in next season's Champions League and are currently in fifth position, three points behind Aston Villa, who are in fourth and have played one extra fixture.
Spurs are in good form and have collected three wins from their last four.
However, they had to come from behind against relegation-threatened Luton Town in their previous outing to avoid a shock defeat that would have put a massive dent in their top-four ambitions.

The score was level late on after an own goal from Issa Kabore cancelled out Tahith Chong's early opener, but Tottenham prevailed thanks to Son Heung-min, who struck his 160th Spurs goal in the 86th minute to help his side to all three points.
Ange Postecoglou's men will be eager to end the campaign strongly and can focus on the league as they are out of the FA Cup and are not in Europe.
West Ham make one change to the side that lost 4-3 to Newcastle in their previous Premier League outing.
Alphonse Areola was forced off against the Magpies with a groin problem and is not in the squad, meaning Fabianski comes in to start in goal.
Spurs make three alterations to the team that came from behind to beat Luton 2-1 in their last match.
Van de Ven was an unused substitute against the Hatters but appears at centre-back instead of Dragusin.
Bentancur comes into the midfield and replaces Sarr, with Johnson appearing on the wing ahead of Kulusevski.
West Ham are looking to achieve a Premier League double over Tottenham for the third time, previously doing so in 1998-99 and 2013-14.
Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Tottenham get this Premier League clash under way.
There is some heavy rain coming down at London Stadium.
Soucek shows his intentions in the first two minutes with a heavy tackle on Bissouma.
The Spurs midfielder stays on the floor for a few seconds before returning to his feet.
Coufal and Bowen combine with a clever one-two down the right, with the full-back getting close to the touchline before sliding a pass inside to Antonio, but Romero gets across to intercept it.
HUGE CHANCE! What an opportunity for West Ham.
Kudus steals possession on the left and gets into a dangerous position before cutting the ball across the box to Bowen.
The England international arrives in the middle, but he shoots wide.
GOALLLL! 1-0 SPURS! The visitors make the lead! Bentancur slots a pass down the left to Werner, who pushes the ball past his marker to get to the byline.
He drives a low cross into Johnson, with the winger scoring from close range.
What an assist from Werner! The Germany International shows his speed to get past a West Ham defender before cutting the ball back across the box.
Johnson darts inside and has the easiest of finishes.
OVER! Bowen's cross is not dealt with by the Spurs defence, with the ball dropping to Kudus in the middle of the box.
He gets a shot away, but it deflects off Romero and goes over the bar.
WIDE! So close from Porro! Spurs retain possession well on the edge of West Ham's box, with the ball rolling across to the Spaniard.
He has time and space to get a shot away, driving his low, right-footed effort just wide of the left post.
Spurs have avoided defeat in their last six matches when scoring the opening goal in the Premier League dating back to December 7 2023.
However, Moyes will take encouragement from the fact that their previous defeat in that run came against West Ham, with the Irons winning 2-1.
SAVE! Spurs are dominating at the moment.
Son receives the ball on the edge of the box and shifts it onto his right foot.
The captain then attempts to curl a right-footed shot on target, with Fabianski getting down to his left to make a simple save.
Son probably should’ve done better, especially with his quality.
Werner has the beating of Coufal on the left, surging past the full-back inside the box before looking to drive a low cross into the middle.
The ball bobbles around before the West Ham defence hack it clear.
Udogie makes a bursting run down the left and is pushed in the back by Paqueta.
The referee tries to let the play continue before blowing for a free-kick.
Maddison's cross from the right is then headed clear.
GOALLLL! ZOUMA SCORES! 1-1! West Ham are level! The Hammers haven’t threatened much in the attack, but find an equaliser through a corner.
Bowen's inswinging cross from the left is met by Zouma, who flicks a header across the goal and into the corner.

events.action: flicks a header across the goal and into the corner

text: Ward-Prowse usually takes the corners for West Ham, but Bowen shows his crossing ability and gets an assist to his name.
His ball into the box is perfect for Zouma, who uses the pace on it to direct his effort past Vicario.
Tottenham have lost three of their last five Premier League London derby matches (winning two), as many as they had in their previous 19 (winning 10 and drawing six).
In the competition’s history, Spurs have conceded 398 goals in such games, and could be the second side to ship 400 after West Ham.
They have dominated the early exchanges, but missed a few chances to double their lead and were punished.
Spurs have controlled possession since conceding and are just trying to stop West Ham from building any momentum.
The home fans in the London Stadium are bouncing, with Kudus getting a loud cheer every time he collects the ball.
Bowen gets the better of Bissouma, who kicks the back of his leg and gives away a free-kick just inside West Ham's half.
Paqueta tries to trick his way into Spurs' box, but runs into a crowd and is tackled.
The ball rebounds out to Bowen, with the winger getting a shot away.
However, his effort takes a deflection on the way through, with Vicario scrambling across to stop it from going out for a corner.
Maddison keeps dropping deep to collect possession, trying to make things happen for Spurs.
He makes a run forward before sliding a pass down the right to Johnson, but his low cross is cleared away.
CHANCE! What a cross from Johnson.
Porro collects possession on the touchline and pokes a pass through to Johnson, who flashes a brilliant cross into the box.
Werner is at the back post, but he doesn’t make a run across.
That should've been a chance for Werner to score, but he didn't anticipate it.
Werner has had five goal involvements in the Premier League this season in 10 games, as many as in his last Premier League season (2021-22) in 21 games.
He has certainly made an impact for Spurs, but still lacks an instinct to score goals.
Maddison continues to drop deep, assessing his options before curling a pass over to Porro on the right.
The full-back sends an inviting cross into the box, but Son is nudged out the way of the ball, allowing Fabianski to collect it.
Romero dives into Bowen outside Spurs' box and gives away a needless free-kick in a shooting position.
Ward-Prowse's right-footed effort is on target, but its a good height for Vicario, who pushes it away.
Antonio uses his physical strength to push past Udogie on the right before challenging Van de Ven, who bundles him to the floor and pokes the ball out for a throw-in.
Antonio thinks he should have a free-kick and is furious with the assistant referee.
Bowen takes another corner on the right, getting an assist with his previous one.
His ball into the box has plenty of pace on it, but Udogie does well to head it clear.
Bowen's third corner from the right is dangerous, with the winger whipping a cross towards the back post.
Vicario does brilliantly to flick it away under pressure.
West Ham are ending the half strongly.
There has been a spree of West Ham corners, with Kudus winning one on the left this time.
Ward-Prowse gets a chance to show his ability, but Udogie does well again to knock it away from Soucek.
Paqueta thunders into Maddison in Spurs' half, leaving the midfielder on the floor.
The Brazilian tries to apologise to Maddison, who is having none of it.
The first yellow card goes to Van de Ven after the defender pushes the ball away from Antonio to stop the play from getting back under way quickly.
Its a soft booking, but that’s the rules.
There will be two minutes of additional time.
Porro is over a corner on the right, with his flat, outswinging cross getting hooked away by Emerson.
Some unusual but effective defending from the Italian.
There is a few Spurs corners to end the half.
Maddison's outswinging cross is headed away by Zouma as far as Bentancur, who whips a right-footed strike wide of the right post.
HALF-TIME: WEST HAM 1-1 TOTTENHAM
Zouma’s header cancelled out Johnson’s opener to send West Ham and Tottenham into half-time with the score level at 1-1.
Bowen had a chance to score inside five minutes, but he directed Kudus' cross wide of the left post.
Instead, Spurs broke the deadlock.
Werner made a fantastic run down the left and cut the ball across to Johnson, who had a simple finish from close range.
Porro then struck his low shot wide of the left post before the Hammers equalised.
Bowen's inswinging corner from the right found Zouma, who flicked his effort across the goal and into the net.
West Ham narrowly edged the first half, creating an xG (expected goals) of 0.61 from their five shots.

Bowen and Kudus has constantly caused problems down the wings with their pace and trickery, but Paqueta has had a quiet half by his standards, completely just 80 per cent of his passes and giving away three fouls.
As for Spurs, they were excellent until they conceded.
Porro and Udogie have supported their attacks brilliantly, constantly causing problems with their overlapping runs.

Bentancur has also been strong in the midfield and has had 66 touches, but there has been some frustration from Maddison, who has constantly dropped deep to collect possession and ended the half on the wrong side of a heavy tackle from Paqueta.
West Ham get the ball rolling again.
They are unbeaten in their last six Premier League matches, winning four (drawing two) when level at the break.
Bowen tries to get past Udogie on the right, but the Spurs defender gets ahead of the winger before getting tripped.
Bowen throws his hands into the air and is furious, but it was a foul.
SAVE! Good stop from Vicario to keep the score level! Ward-Prowse makes the most of a loose pass from Bentancur on the edge of Spurs' box and offloads the ball to Antonio.
He gets a shot away on his left foot, but his curling effort is pushed away by Vicario.
OFFSIDE! Bowen puts another delightful corner into the box on the right, with the winger whipping a cross into a dangerous area.
Mavropanos sends a downward header on target, but Vicario blocks it on the line before the flag goes up for offside against Antonio.
He was blocking the goalkeeper.
WIDE! West Ham are having all the chances at the moment.
Paqueta uses his trickery to roll past Bentancur on the edge of the box before curling a left-footed effort just wide of the left post.
It feels like the Hammers are getting closer and closer to taking the lead.
Ward-Prowse is over a free-kick on the right, and he whips a cross into the box towards the back post.
However, he puts too much pace on it, with Soucek unable to keep the attack alive.
Antonio is shown a yellow card after stepping on Bentancur.
He was stretching for the ball and is unlucky, but his tackle was worth a booking.
Johnson made a huge impact with his crosses off the bench against Luton in Spurs' last match, registering as assist for Son's winning goal.
His low ball into the box from the right is fantastic, but it goes past Son and Werner before bouncing away from danger.
WIDE! Nice move from Spurs.
Porro, Maddison and Bentancur combine with some quick passing on the edge of the box before Ward-Prowse clears it away as far as Bissouma.
He has time and space on the edge of the box, but whips his right-footed strike wide of the right post.
Bowen shows brilliant determination to get past Udogie on the right before flicking a pass inside to Paqueta, who lashes his shot from distance high and wide of the target.
Bowen really sets the tempo for the Hammers.
West Ham have conceded at least once in each of their last 10 Premier League games, shipping 24 goals in total in this run.

Their 55 goals conceded overall this season is just one fewer than they shipped in the whole of last term, while only in 2010-11 (1.84) have they had a higher goals conceded per game average than their 1.8 so far in 2023-24.
Spurs are having a good spell of possession, but are struggling to break the Hammers' rigid defensive structure.
SAVE! Antonio simply must score! West Ham counter brilliantly, with Antonio and Van de Ven getting into a battle after Ward-Prowse sends the ball over the top.
The West Ham forward muscles Van de Ven to the floor and is one-on-one with Vicario, but sends his shot straight at the goalkeeper.
He won’t get a better chance than that!
Bentancur is the latest player to go into the book for a foul.
Son has been quiet on his 400th appearance for Spurs.
He has only had 26 touches and one shot, with most of the attacking play coming down the wings.
OVER! A rare chance for Son! Maddison switches the ball over to Son, who shifts possession onto his right foot inside the box before crashing his shot well over the bar.
The tempo has dropped in the last couple of minutes, with the possession switching sides constantly.
Sarr has been waiting to come on for some time, but the ball hasn’t gone off the pitch!
Everyone is back for West Ham, with the hosts crowding the edge of their own box to stop shots from reaching their goal.
After Johnson has his effort blocked, Porro sneaks a low strike through a number of bodies, but it goes straight at Fabianski.
Bentancur is on his way off after having 92 touches, more than any other player.
Sarr takes his place in the midfield.
Maddison grew into the second half but still struggled to create anything for Spurs in a central position.
He is replaced by Kulusevski.
Kulusevski gets involved immediately after coming on.
He plays a clever one-two with Son on the edge of the box, allowing the South Korea international to move into space before laying a pass into Johnson.
However, his low cross from the right is blocked.
WHAT A CROSS! Spurs are pushing for a second goal! Johnson and Porro work together on the right before playing a pass out to Sarr, who whips a phenomenal low cross into a dangerous area.
It looks like Werner will have an easy finish, but Coufal gets back to clear it away.
Johnson goes into the book after tripping Kudus just inside West Ham's half.

Tottenham are winless in their last three Premier League away games against West Ham (drawing one and losing two), their longest run without a win at the Hammers since a run of six between 1995 and 2001.
They look like the team more likely to take the lead, but must put Fabianski under more pressure.
Spurs have only had one shot on target in the second half and are not making the most of their dominance.
Johnson has been reliable with his crosses from the right, but lofts the ball straight into Fabianski's gloves this time.
West Ham are putting plenty of players behind the ball to defend, which is making it difficult for Spurs to create opportunities.
Spurs are having all of the possession but are cannot make anything with it.
Porro looks to create a chance with a cross from the right towards Sarr, but the ball is flicked away from his head by Werner, who is in an offside position.
Tottenham are making two changes to try and get a second goal.
Werner has been quiet in the second half and is being replaced by Richarlison.
The Brazilian will go up front, with Son moving over to the left.
Hojbjerg also replaces Bissouma in a straight swap in the midfield.
Antonio drifts out to the left and shows some pace to push the ball past Porro before driving a cross straight into Vicario's gloves.
Ings is getting ready to come on for the hosts.
Paqueta curls a pass down the right to Bowen, who wins a corner off Van de Ven.
Bowen's inswinging cross has plenty of pace, but it flicks off Soucek before going out for a goal-kick.
PENALTY SHOUT! Son gets a chance to run at his marker down the left before sliding a pass through to Hojbjerg, who has his cross blocked by Coufal.
He wants a penalty for handball, but it clearly hit his chest.
Romero is the fourth player to go into the book for Spurs after a foul on Ward-Prowse.
The hosts try to take it quickly, but the referee stops the play.
Johnson looks like he is hurt and is slowly walking off the pitch, with Lo Celso taking his place for the final few minutes.
There will be four minutes of additional time.
Ward-Prowse is over a late corner on the left for West Ham.
His inswinging cross is whipped towards the back post, but Vicario gets through a crowd to punch it away.
SAVE! Chance for Spurs to win it! The visitors take their time in possession around West Ham's box before Porro decides to curl a left-footed cross into the box from the left.
Lo Celso flicks it to Udogie, but he drives his low strike straight at Fabianski.
FULL-TIME: WEST HAM 1-1 TOTTENHAM
Tottenham missed the chance to move into fourth position in the Premier League after a 1-1 draw with West Ham at London Stadium.
Spurs took the lead inside five minutes through Johnson, who scored his fifth goal of the season from close range after getting onto Werner's low cross.
However, the visitors couldn’t add to their lead, with the Hammers levelling later in the first half.
Zouma latched onto Bowen's inswinging corner from the right and directed his effort across the goal and into the net.
Both teams then missed huge chances to win it.
Antonio did brilliantly to get away from Van de Ven, but he struck his shot straight at Vicario.
Udogie then had an opportunity for Spurs deep into stoppage time, but his low effort was stopped by Fabianski.
It was a very close contest, with West Ham creating an xG of 1.16 compared to Tottenham's 0.96.
Next, the Irons travel to Wolves, with Spurs hosting Nottingham Forest.
That's all for today, goodbye.
